items.description:
Pakistan, along with seven other Arab and Muslim countries, on Wednesday welcomed the United Kingdom’s decision to ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
UK imposed the trade measures on Tuesday, alongside Canada and France. The decision was announced by British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who accused the Israeli government of turning a “blind eye” to what he called “ethnic cleansing” by settlers in the West Bank.

items.title: Two navy personnel martyred while patrolling at sea: DGPR
items.description:
Two Pakistan Navy personnel were martyred while patrolling at sea to ensure security, the Navy’s Directorate-General of Public Relations (DGPR) said on Wednesday.
“Shoaibur Rehman (PMA-IV) and Ghufran Nasar (PMT-II) embraced martyrdom while performing patrolling duties at sea to ensure security,” it said in a statement on X.
As per the statement, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf expressed deep sorrow over the loss of precious lives.
“Senior Pakistan Navy officials attended the funerals of martyred sailors and met their families,” it added.

items.title: Islamabad admin announces 'complete ban' on sheesha cafes as IHC gives a month to formulate regulations
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: Islamabad Deputy Commissioner (DC) Irfan Nawaz Memon on Wednesday announced a “complete” ban on running sheesha cafes in the federal capital.
“Immediately implementing the Islamabad High Court’s order, a complete ban has been imposed on running sheesha cafes in the federal capital until further orders,” the DC posted on X.

items.description:
RAWALPINDI: The body of a lawyer was found inside a car at the Judicial Complex’s parking lot on Wednesday, police said.
According to the initial police report, a moharir at the judicial complex informed Civil Lines police about the body at around 9:30am.

A Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) team was also called to the scene, it added.

items.title: Bangladesh fights world's worst measles outbreak as vaccination gaps fuel spread
items.description:
Bangladesh, which once came close to eliminating measles, is facing its worst outbreak on record, with 999 suspected and confirmed measles-related deaths reported since March as hospitals struggle with overcrowding, shortages and a continuing influx of sick children.

items.title: Exchange companies’ dollar sales jump 30pc
items.description:
KARACHI: Exchange companies’ dollar sales to banks increased by 30 per cent year-on-year in August, indicating higher inflows.
Data from the Exchange Companies Association of Pakistan (ECAP) showed these companies sold $248.7 million to banks in August, up from $174.9m in the same month last year.
However, July saw a decline to $230.7m, down from $290.6m in the corresponding month last year.
Pakistan has remained unaffected by the Gulf war as far as remittances are concerned, but reports in the media that Pakistani workers are being sent back home from Gulf countries have caused fear.
